Exposure to compliance with government regulations, intellectual property disputes and contractual obligations; failure to comply with legal requirements or contractual obligations could significantly impact business, reputation and financial performance.
Failure to keep pace with evolving technology in the corn wet-milling industry could impact competitiveness in efficiency, waste reduction and product quality.

Growing customer demand for sustainable sourcing and production processes is a market risk; customers increasingly evaluate suppliers on sustainability and environment parameters in addition to price and quality.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Favourable long-term demand for maize-based products across diverse end-user industries such as food processing, FMCG, pharmaceuticals, textiles, paper, adhesives, packaging and cattle feed
- Management expects demand for the Company's products to remain healthy given continued steady growth of the Indian economy
- Rebalancing of US trade tariffs has created a more level playing field for Indian exporters, and the Company has begun witnessing improved enquiry levels in export markets
- Alland & Sayaji LLP is setting up its second spray-drying plant for gum arabic powder, and Nigay & Sayaji LLP is establishing its caramel colours manufacturing facility (using the Company's dextrose syrup as feedstock), both expected to expand the Company's addressable revenue and margin pool
- The commissioning of the Company's 4.5 MW solar power plant is expected to contribute to lower energy costs and increased use of renewable energy, improving cost competitiveness
- Growth of the Indian corn starch market driven by rising urbanisation, changing consumer lifestyles, disposable incomes and consumption of processed/convenience foods, with the pharmaceutical sector emerging as one of the fastest-growing application segments

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company proposes to gradually increase its maize grinding capacity in future through modernization of equipment, expected to improve the top and bottom lines. It has undertaken a Technology Modernisation and Automation project targeted for completion by September 2027 and a Product Upgradation Project targeted for completion by June 2027, both aimed at process optimization, debottlenecking, modernization of manufacturing facilities and improving production efficiencies. Growth capacity is also being added through the group's joint ventures/subsidiaries: Alland & Sayaji LLP is setting up its second spray-drying plant for gum arabic powder, and Nigay & Sayaji LLP is establishing a caramel colours manufacturing facility (a new 50:50 JV with Nigay SAS, France) that will use the Company's dextrose syrup as feedstock.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- scale: among the largest corn refiners in India with an annual capacity of 1,000 Metric Tonnes Per Day (MTPD) — evidence: 'the Company is amongst the largest corn refiners in India. With an annual capacity of 1000 Metric Tonnes Per Day (MTPD), the Company among the foremost corn starch producers in the country'
- distribution: established export franchise with Export House Status and a wide domestic distribution network — evidence: 'the Company has a market in more than 40 countries and is one of the big exporters in India's starch industry. Its commendable export work has been credited with the Export House Status by the government of India. Besides, the Company has a strong distribution network in India, with branches and agents'
- technology: technical collaboration with established international process-technology partners — evidence: 'The company has continued to avail the benefits of technical expertise from M/s Tate & Lyle, Belgium and SIGMA Mudhendislik Makine Sanayi Ve Ticaret ... Turkey. This has enabled it to further improve the technical parameters of the production processes and also improve the quality of its products'
- cost position: captive/renewable power generation meeting a large majority of power needs, lowering energy cost — evidence: 'Together with the existing captive steam turbines and gas engine, the Company now meets approximately 86% of its total power requirement through captive generation, with solar power offering an estimated energy cost saving of over 50% as compared to grid power'

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The corn starch industry is witnessing increased capacity expansion by existing players, entry of new players and growing availability of substitute materials; higher domestic maize prices vs. steady international maize prices is pressuring the Company's pricing in export markets and may impact export market share.
- Maize, an agricultural product, is highly vulnerable to climate change — droughts, floods, heatwaves, pests and diseases can disrupt corn production, causing shortages and higher production costs, with power costs also affected by input-cost dynamics.
- Increasing regulation and changing government policy on sustainability and climate change (including India's NDC targets) could result in fines, legal action and reputational damage if the Company fails to comply.
- As a company based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, the Company is exposed to acute physical risks such as floods, droughts, storms, fires and heavy rains that could affect manufacturing facilities, inventory, supply chain and delivery.
- Exposure to compliance with government regulations, intellectual property disputes and contractual obligations; failure to comply with legal requirements or contractual obligations could significantly impact business, reputation and financial performance.
- Failure to keep pace with evolving technology in the corn wet-milling industry could impact competitiveness in efficiency, waste reduction and product quality.
- Growing customer demand for sustainable sourcing and production processes is a market risk; customers increasingly evaluate suppliers on sustainability and environment parameters in addition to price and quality.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Increasing the share of value-added products in the portfolio
- Strengthening presence in domestic as well as international markets
- Enhancing customer relationships and improving product realizations
- Exploring new market opportunities and expanding export business to diversify the revenue base
- Operational excellence through process optimizations, debottlenecking and modernization of manufacturing facilities to enhance product quality, maximize yield and reduce operating costs
- Growing the speciality food ingredients businesses (via the JV/subsidiary structure) as a key growth driver
- Efficient working capital management and prudent capital allocation
